title: Slovenia vs Scotland: Pocognoli's Nations League Debut
seoTitle: Slovenia vs Scotland: Pocognoli's Nations League Debut
subtitle: The clash marks the start of their League B campaign and a test of new leaders
excerpt: The Slovenia vs Scotland match on September 26, 2026, features Sébastien Pocognoli's debut for Scotland and the absence of key players.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The match between Slovenia and Scotland, scheduled for September 26, 2026, draws attention as it brings together two national teams entering a restructuring phase. In Slovenia, the absence of Benjamin Sesko due to a shin injury and other injured players opens up space for youngsters like Andraz Sporar and Vipotnik. In Scotland, the debut of coach Sébastien Pocognoli, who replaced Steve Clarke, and the call-up of seven players without international experience make the game a test of new leadership.

Slovenia: Absences and Focus on Experience

The Slovenian national team arrives for the match with a history of inconsistent performance in recent games, alternating draws and losses, and counting on only one recent victory. Benjamin Sesko's injury, which left the team without its main striker, weighs on the offensive sector. Other absences include Zan Zaletel and Nik Prelec, both sidelined due to injury. Goalkeeper Jan Oblak, who is about to complete 85 games for the national team, remains a defensive pillar. In the market, the hosts are considered favorites, with odds of 2.50 for a Slovenian victory, 3.00 for a draw, and 2.88 for a Scottish victory. Betting on over 2.5 goals has odds of 2.25, while both teams to score has 1.94.

Scotland: New Phase and Renewed Players

The Scottish national team takes the field after Steve Clarke's departure and the arrival of Sébastien Pocognoli, who makes his debut against Slovenia. The coach called up 14 players who were absent from the World Cup and seven athletes without international caps. Among the absentees, Kieran Tierney and Kenny McLean are injured, as are other players such as Shankland, Che Adams, McTominay, and McLean. The goals market indicates under 2.5 at 1.61. In recent history, Scotland has experienced a positive spell, with three consecutive victories before this round. Betting on a Scottish victory comes in at 2.88.

The Match at Stadion Stožice

The game will be held at Stadion Stožice, in Ljubljana, at 10 AM Brasília time, and will be broadcast live on Disney+. Slovenia hosts Scotland at home, where they have a solid record, having not lost in 35 of their last 41 home games. The match sets the tone for both teams' aspirations in League B, where the first round already marks the start of their campaigns and their future regarding relegation or staying in the competition.

Qualification Context and Future Challenges

For Slovenia, the Nations League represents an opportunity to consolidate a competitive group after failing to qualify for the 2026 World Cup. The team finished third in Group B during the qualifiers and in the 2024/25 Nations League, needing to play playoffs to remain in League B. Scotland, having returned to League B after being relegated in the previous edition, seeks to avoid further relegations and take advantage of the new phase under Pocognoli. The clash also serves to evaluate the new generation of players, such as Adam Gnezda Čerin and Benjamin Šeško, who have been gaining prominence in Slovenia. In Scotland's case, the players called up without international experience are a bet on the future for the national team.

Market Expectations and Betting

Betting markets reflect the relative balance between the three outcomes. A Slovenian victory has odds of 2.50, a draw at 3.00, and a Scottish victory at 2.88. The goals market indicates under 2.5 at 1.61, while over 2.5 has odds of 2.25. Bets on both teams to score have odds of 1.94. These values show that, despite differences in form and absences, bettors see the game as balanced with chances for both sides to win.

With information from NETVASCO, VAVEL.com.
